title: Technology Sector Update for 05/03/2018: NXPI,LOGI,NSIT,CRUS

Technology stocks were recovering from earlier declines Thursday afternoon, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 ( XLK ) edging up 0.1% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index ( SOX ) was posting a 0.5% gain.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ) fell to its lowest share price since September 2016 at $90.83 a share after the chipmaker reported lower Q1 earnings and weaker-than-expected revenues for the January-to-March fiscal period. It earned $0.17 per share, down sharply compared with a $3.79 per share profit during the same quarter last year and trailing the Capital IQ consensus expecting GAAP net income of $0.39 per share. Revenue rose to $2.27 billion from $2.21 billion last year but also missed the $2.34 billion Street view.
In other sector news:
+ Insight Enterprises ( NSIT ) soared nearly 23% at one point Thursday after reporting Q1 net income and revenue exceeding Wall Street estimates and raised its FY18 earnings forecast above Street views. Excluding one-time items, the enterprise software firm earned $0.94 per share, topping the Capital IQ consensus for normalized earnings by $0.34 per share. Net sales rose 19% year over year to $1.76 billion, topping the $1.53 billion analyst mean. Looking forward, Insight increased its projected FY18 EPS outlook by $0.45 compared with its prior forecast to a new range of $4.35 to $4.45 per share, surpassing the consensus estimate by at least $0.39 per share.
+ Logitech International ( LOGI ) climbed almost 10% on Thursday after the computer peripherals company exceeded analyst estimates with its Q4 financial results. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.32 per share during the three months ended March 31, up from $0.30 per share during the same quarter last year and topping the Capital IQ consensus by $0.08 per share. Revenue rose to $592.4 million from $510.6 million last year, also beating the $560.4 million analyst mean. Logitech Thursday also confirmed its FY19 outlook expecting sales growth in the high single percentage digits. Analysts, on average, are expecting FY18 sales at the company to rise 14.1% over the prior 12-month period to around $2.53 billion.
+ Cirrus Logic (CRUS) has turned fractionally higher this afternoon, erasing a nearly 9% decline earlier Thursday that followed the fabless chipmaker reporting below-consensus fiscal Q4 financial results and forecasting revenue for the current quarter also trailing Wall Street expectations. Excluding one-time items, it earned $0.51 per share, down from $0.85 per share last year and missing the Capital IQ consensus by $0.07 per share. Revenue fell to $303.2 million from $327.9 million last year and also lagging the $316.6 million Street view. For the current quarter, the company is modelling Q1 revenue between $210 million to $250 million. Analysts, on average, are looking for $294.7 million in revenue in the April-to-June reporting period.
